name: Judit Polgár
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest chess Grandmaster in history at age 15 in 1991, breaking Bobby Fischer's 33-year-old record, after winning the boys' World Youth Chess Championship at ages 12 and 14 and Olympic gold with Hungary in 1988 at age 12.
early_history_summary: Judit Polgár was the youngest of three sisters raised in Budapest as part of a deliberate educational experiment by her father László Polgár, a psychologist who believed any child could be raised to be a genius through early intensive specialization. She was homeschooled with chess as the primary focus, studying 8 hours a day alongside her sisters, and began playing tournaments at age 9, winning her first international tournament at the New York Open.
family_context_summary: Daughter of László Polgár, a Hungarian psychologist and educational theorist, and Klara Polgár, a teacher; parents deliberately designed a homeschooling experiment to raise prodigies, choosing chess as the specialization field; family was of modest means but dedicated all resources to the children's chess education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Judit's father László Polgár was a psychologist who authored 'Bring Up Genius!' and designed the entire educational experiment around chess, homeschooling his daughters with 8 hours of daily chess study and hiring professional GM trainers including Pal Benko and Alexander Chernin.
evidence_summary: Judit Polgár was the product of a deliberate educational experiment by her father László Polgár, a psychologist who believed geniuses are made not born and chose chess as the vehicle. She was homeschooled from birth with 8 hours of daily chess study, surrounded by her two older sisters who were also competitive chess players, creating an exceptional peer training environment. The family hired professional grandmaster trainers including Pal Benko and Alexander Chernin, and the home was filled with chess books and 30 boards pinned to the wall. By 5 she could beat her father, by 9 she won an international tournament, by 12 she won Olympic gold, and at 15 she became the youngest grandmaster ever. The communist regime's resistance to homeschooling added urgency. Her path was entirely shaped by her father's domain expertise and educational design.

name: Jan Timman
milestone_by_age_26: Attained the Grandmaster title in 1974 at age 22, becoming the Netherlands' third Grandmaster after Max Euwe and Jan Hein Donner, and won the Dutch Chess Championship for the first time in the same year. By age 26 he had also won international tournaments at Hastings 1973-74, Sombor 1974, Netanya 1975, and Reykjavik 1976.
early_history_summary: Timman was born in Amsterdam, the son of mathematics professor Reinier Timman and his wife Anneke, who as a schoolgirl was a mathematics student of former world champion Max Euwe. He learned chess at 8, came fourth in the Dutch Junior (under-20) Championship at 12, became junior champion at 14, and finished third at the World Junior Championship in Jerusalem at 15. He received the International Master title in 1971 at 19 and the Grandmaster title in 1974 at 22.
family_context_summary: Timman was born in Amsterdam, the son of mathematics professor Reinier Timman and his wife Anneke, who as a schoolgirl was a mathematics student of former world champion Max Euwe. His older brother Ton (1948-2014) held the chess title of FIDE Master. The family had a strong academic and chess background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Timman's family had significant chess domain expertise: his mother was a student of former world champion Max Euwe, his father was a mathematics professor (closely related to chess aptitude), and his older brother Ton was a FIDE Master. This created a family-domain apprenticeship environment where chess was embedded in daily life.
evidence_summary: Timman's chess development was deeply embedded in his family environment: his mother studied under former world champion Max Euwe, his father was a mathematics professor, and his older brother was a FIDE Master who introduced him to chess and provided early competitive pressure. He showed prodigy-level talent (fourth in Dutch Junior Championship at 12, champion at 14, World Junior bronze at 15) and achieved Grandmaster status at 22. The family's academic and chess background provided both domain expertise and a network connection to the Dutch chess elite through Max Euwe. His father's professorship provided modest financial stability.
starting_point: Born in Amsterdam in 1951 to a mathematics professor father and a mother who had been a student of former world champion Max Euwe; learned chess from his older brother Ton, a FIDE Master.
current_position: Died on February 18, 2026 at age 74 in Arnhem, Netherlands; final role as one of the Netherlands' most celebrated chess grandmasters and chess authors.

His father was a well-known literary editor and his mother designed women's hats. He entered the Tokyo National University of Fine Arts and Music in 1970, earning a BA in music composition in 1974 and an MA in 1976 with emphasis on electronic and ethnic music. He began working as a session musician with Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi in 1977, leading to the formation of YMO in 1978.

His father's position as a literary editor provided a cultured home environment. The key catalyst was meeting Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi as a session musician in 1977, leading to YMO's formation in 1978. The electronic music wave of the late 1970s provided a structural tailwind for his innovative work.
starting_point: Born in Tokyo in 1952 to a renowned editor father who shaped postwar Japanese literature; began piano at age three and studied composition at Tokyo National University of Fine Arts and Music.

name: Michael Schumacher
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Formula One debut with Jordan at the 1991 Belgian Grand Prix at age 22, qualifying seventh, which led to Benetton signing him immediately; by age 25 he won his first World Drivers' Championship in 1994 and defended it in 1995.
early_history_summary: Born in Hürth, West Germany to a working-class family, Schumacher began competitive kart racing at age four in a pedal kart his father built from discarded parts. His parents took him to the Kerpen-Horrem karting track where he became the youngest club member. He obtained a Luxembourg kart license at 12 to circumvent German age rules, won the German Junior Kart Championship at 14, and the European Kart Championship at 18 in 1987. He dominated Formula König in 1988, won the German Formula Three Championship and Macau Grand Prix in 1990, and joined the Mercedes-Benz junior sportscar program before his F1 debut in 1991.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Hürth. Father worked at a karting track and built Schumacher's first kart from discarded parts, taking a second job renting and repairing karts. Mother worked at the track's canteen. Parents could not afford new engines; local businessmen provided financial support to continue racing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father modified a pedal kart with a motorcycle engine and built karts from discarded parts, worked at the karting track, and took a second job to support racing. Mother worked at the track canteen. Total family immersion in the karting environment, though not professional racing background.
evidence_summary: Schumacher's extraordinary racing career was built on early and total immersion in karting from age four, supported by a working-class family that sacrificed financially to enable his participation. His father built karts from discarded parts and both parents worked at the local karting track. Despite financial constraints (parents couldn't afford new engines), he progressed through the German karting system, won the European Championship at 18, and was recruited into the Mercedes-Benz junior program. Manager Willi Weber funded his Formula Three career, leading to his F1 debut at 22 and World Championship at 25.
starting_point: Born in Hurth, West Germany to a bricklayer father who ran the local kart track and a mother who operated the canteen; modest family background.
current_position: Living in Switzerland; health status closely guarded by family following a severe brain injury from a skiing accident in December 2013.

name: Susan Polgár
milestone_by_age_26: Became the top-ranked female chess player in the world on the FIDE Elo rating list of July 1984 at age 15, the youngest ever to achieve the world #1 ranking. She won the World Under-16 Girls Championship in 1981 at age 12 and earned the Grandmaster title in 1991 at age 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest in 1969, Susan Polgár was the eldest of three daughters in an educational experiment by her father László Polgár, who believed 'geniuses are made, not born.' She and her sisters were homeschooled with chess as the principal subject. She won her first tournament at age 4 (the Budapest Girls' Under-11 Championship with a 10-0 score), won the World Under-16 Girls Championship at 12, and became the world's top-rated female player at 15 in 1984. Despite FIDE restrictions on her participation, she earned the Grandmaster title in 1991.
family_context_summary: Father László Polgár was an educator who designed a deliberate experiment to prove children could achieve exceptional results through specialized training from an early age. Mother Klara was a teacher. Both grandmothers were Holocaust survivors. The family was Hungarian-Jewish of modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father László Polgár conceived and executed a systematic educational program with chess as the principal subject, homeschooling all three daughters. He was the primary coach and mentor, designing the entire curriculum around chess mastery from age 4. His thesis was that 'geniuses are made, not born.'
evidence_summary: Susan Polgár's early chess dominance was the product of her father László Polgár's deliberate educational experiment, which immersed all three daughters in chess from age 4 as the principal subject of homeschooling. She won her first tournament at 4 with a perfect 10-0 score, the World Under-16 Girls Championship at 12, and became the world's top-rated female player at 15. Her two sisters (Judit and Sofia) also became elite chess players, creating a unique high-trust peer environment. FIDE's gender-based restrictions on her tournament participation created adversity that may have sharpened her determination.
starting_point: Born in Budapest, Hungary in 1969 to Laszlo Polgar, who deliberately educated his three daughters in chess from early childhood as an educational experiment; homeschooled with chess as the primary subject.
current_position: Lives in suburban St. Louis, Missouri; serves as head of the Susan Polgar Institute for Chess Excellence (SPICE) and coaches collegiate chess.

name: Robin Williams
milestone_by_age_26: Made his national television debut on the 1977 NBC special The Great American Laugh Off and the Laugh-In revival series (1977-1978) at age 26, discovered by TV producer George Schlatter at the Comedy Store in Los Angeles, which led directly to his casting as Mork in Mork & Mindy (1978).
early_history_summary: Born in Chicago in 1951, Williams grew up in an affluent suburban family (father was a Ford senior executive). He attended private Detroit Country Day School, then Redwood High School in California. He studied theater at College of Marin for three years before earning a full scholarship to Juilliard in 1973, where he was one of two students (with Christopher Reeve) selected by John Houseman for the Advanced Program. He left Juilliard in 1976 and began performing stand-up at the Holy City Zoo in San Francisco, then moved to LA's Comedy Store where he was discovered by Schlatter in 1977.
family_context_summary: Father Robert Fitzgerald Williams was a senior executive in Ford's Lincoln-Mercury Division. Mother Laurie McLaurin was a former model whose great-grandfather was Mississippi senator and governor Anselm J. McLaurin. Family lived in a 40-room farmhouse on 20 acres in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. Comfortable upper-middle-class upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a corporate executive at Ford, not in entertainment. Mother was a former model. No direct family domain advantage in comedy or acting, though the family's social status provided access to private education and cultural exposure.
evidence_summary: Williams benefited from an affluent upbringing (father a Ford executive) that provided private schooling, and from elite training at Juilliard on full scholarship, where John Houseman selected him for the Advanced Program. The key catalyst was the San Francisco 'comedy renaissance' of the mid-1970s and the LA Comedy Store scene, which placed him at the frontier of a cultural wave. His extraordinary improvisational ability was recognized early by peers and teachers. The transition from stand-up to national TV via Schlatter's Laugh-In special in 1977 opened the door to Mork & Mindy and stardom.
starting_point: Born in Chicago, Illinois to Robert Fitzgerald Williams, a senior executive at Ford Motor Company, and Laurie McLaurin, a former model; raised in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan and Marin County, California; described as a shy, quiet child.
current_position: Died on August 11, 2014 at age 63 in Paradise Cay, California; autopsy revealed diffuse Lewy body disease; final films included Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb (2014).

He became one of the world's best junior players, winning the boys' singles at both the French Open and Wimbledon in 1978.

He won junior titles at both Roland-Garros and Wimbledon in 1978 at 18, earning the world #1 junior ranking, then won seven ATP titles in 1980 at 20. His father's profession as a lawyer provided middle-class stability, and the Czech tennis system provided competitive infrastructure. milestone_by_age_26: Won his first French Open title at age 18 in June 1974, the youngest male French Open champion at the time, having already made Sweden's Davis Cup team at 15, won the Wimbledon junior title and Orange Bowl at 16, and turned professional at 16 in 1973.

Davis Cup captain Lennart Bergelin became his primary coach from 1971. At 15, Borg represented Sweden in the Davis Cup; at 16, he won the Wimbledon junior title and turned professional.
family_context_summary: Borg was born in Stockholm, the only child of Rune Borg (1932-2008), an electrician, and Margaretha Borg (b. 1934). He grew up in nearby Sodertalje in a working-class family. His father won a golden tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament and gave it to Borg as a child, beginning his tennis career.

evidence_summary: Borg's tennis career was sparked by his father's gift of a golden tennis racket won at a table-tennis tournament, a serendipitous introduction to the sport at age 9. He showed extraordinary natural ability, beating Sweden's best under-18 players by 13, and was identified by Davis Cup captain Lennart Bergelin, who became his sustained coach from 1971 through his entire professional career. Borg's revolutionary playing style, featuring heavy topspin and a two-handed backhand, was so effective that Bergelin cautioned against anyone changing it. He was a teenage sensation who won the French Open at 18, propelled by the 1970s tennis boom. Despite a working-class background (father was an electrician), his prodigy-level talent and early coaching access drove his rapid ascent.

name: Michael Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: Released 'Thriller' in November 1982 at age 24, which became the best-selling album of all time. early_history_summary: Michael Jackson was born in Gary, Indiana, the eighth of ten children in a working-class African-American family. His father Joe Jackson, a crane operator at US Steel who also played guitar in a local R&B band, organized his sons into a musical group in the early 1960s. Michael began performing at age 5 and joined the Jackson 5 as lead singer. The group played talent shows and the Chitlin' Circuit, signed with Steeltown Records in 1967, then with Motown in 1968. Their first Motown single 'I Want You Back' hit No. 1 in January 1970. Michael launched his solo career with 'Off the Wall' (1979) and released 'Thriller' (1982), the best-selling album of all time.
family_context_summary: Born into a working-class African-American family in Gary, Indiana. Father Joe Jackson was a crane operator at US Steel who also played guitar in a local R&B band and became the Jackson 5's manager. Mother Katherine Jackson was a homemaker and Jehovah's Witness who played clarinet, cello, and piano. The family of ten children lived in a small two-bedroom home. Joe Jackson's management was reportedly physically and emotionally abusive.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Joe Jackson played guitar in a local R&B group (the Falcons) and managed the Jackson 5, providing both musical domain knowledge and relentless training. Mother Katherine was a aspiring musician who played multiple instruments and encouraged the children's musical talents. The entire family was organized around the musical group, making it a family business.
evidence_summary: Michael Jackson's extraordinary career was built on extreme early specialization: he began performing at age 5, was a professional recording artist by 9, and had four No. 1 hits by 12. His father Joe, a steelworker who played guitar in a local R&B band, organized and managed the Jackson 5 with intense (and reportedly abusive) rehearsal regimes. Signing with Motown, the premier Black music label, provided a world-class performance pipeline and national distribution. The Jackson 5 brothers formed a durable high-trust team, and Michael's prodigious vocal and dance talent was recognized from his earliest performances. Despite working-class origins in Gary, Indiana, the combination of family-domain apprenticeship, the Motown platform, and extraordinary natural talent produced the best-selling album of all time by age 24.
starting_point: Born in Gary, Indiana to Joe Jackson, a steel mill worker and former boxer, and Katherine Jackson, a Jehovah's Witness and former musician; eighth of ten children in a working-class African American family.

name: Riccardo Patrese
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut at the 1977 Monaco Grand Prix at age 23, having won both the Italian and European Formula 3 championships in 1976 and the Karting World Championship in 1974 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Patrese was born in Padua, Italy, and started karting at age 7 after his father bought a go-kart in 1961. His father and elder brother were passionate about cars and motorsport. He won the Karting World Championship in 1974 at Estoril, then moved to Formula Italia (1975, finishing second), Formula 3 (1976, winning both Italian and European championships), and Formula 2 (1977) before making his F1 debut at Monaco in 1977. He scored his first F1 point at the Japanese Grand Prix later that year.
secondary_engine: Family support and Italian motorsport pipeline
family_context_summary: Born into a middle-class family in Padua, Italy. Father Mario was a food industry dealer, mother Elena was a school teacher. His father and elder brother Alberto (13 years older, an engineer at Alfa Romeo) were both passionate about cars and motorsport. His father bought a go-kart in 1961 and supported Riccardo's racing career, including fitting out a truck to transport the car for one season.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Mario was passionate about cars and motorsport, bought a go-kart in 1961, and actively supported Riccardo's racing. Brother Alberto, an engineer at Alfa Romeo, shared the passion and first sparked Riccardo's interest. The family discussed racing drivers like 'knights of the round table,' immersing Riccardo in motorsport culture from childhood.
evidence_summary: Patrese's career was built on extreme early specialization in karting, starting at age 7 when his father bought a go-kart in 1961 — unusually early access to racing equipment. trajectory.title: The Lion King and Four Weddings
trajectory.description: Voiced Zazu in Disney's 'The Lion King' and appeared in 'Four Weddings and a Funeral,' expanding his international film profile.

trajectory.title: Bean: The Movie

trajectory.title: Wonka and continued work

name: Kate Bush
milestone_by_age_26: Topped the UK singles chart for four weeks in March 1978 at age 19 with her debut single 'Wuthering Heights,' becoming the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song; her debut album The Kick Inside sold over a million copies.
early_history_summary: Bush began writing songs at age 11, taught herself piano, and grew up in a musical household in Kent. Family friend Ricky Hopper passed her demo to Pink Floyd guitarist David Gilmour, who financed a professional demo recording when she was 16. EMI signed her, gave her a large advance, and she spent two years studying interpretive dance before releasing 'Wuthering Heights' at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Bexleyheath, Kent. Father Paddy was a doctor and amateur pianist; mother was an amateur traditional Irish dancer. Two older brothers were heavily involved in music and poetry. Artistic household that encouraged creative development.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur pianist and mother an amateur Irish dancer; both older brothers were deeply involved in music. Family provided a rich musical environment and supported her artistic development from childhood.
evidence_summary: Bush's extraordinary songwriting talent emerged at 11, but the critical catalyst was David Gilmour of Pink Floyd, who personally financed her professional demo recording and connected her to EMI. Her family was middle-class and deeply musical — father a doctor and pianist, mother a dancer, brothers in music. EMI signed her at 16 and gave her a large advance for dance training. Her debut single 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK chart at 19, making her the first female artist with a self-written number one. The combination of mentorship, family musical environment, and label investment created a uniquely accelerated path.
starting_point: Born in Bexleyheath, Kent to a middle-class family; father Paddy was a doctor and amateur pianist, mother was an amateur Irish dancer; two older brothers deeply involved in music; artistic household that encouraged creative development.
current_position: Living in Devon, England; estimated net worth ~$60 million; largely reclusive but achieved massive resurgence in 2022; inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.

trajectory.title: 'Wuthering Heights' tops UK chart
trajectory.description: Her debut single 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK singles chart for four weeks, making her the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song.

trajectory.title: Never for Ever - first UK number-one album
trajectory.description: Released Never for Ever, which became her first album to top the UK Albums Chart, making her the first British solo female artist to achieve this.

trajectory.title: Hounds of Love
trajectory.description: Released Hounds of Love, her most critically acclaimed and commercially successful album, featuring 'Running Up That Hill' and the conceptual suite The Ninth Wave.

trajectory.title: The Red Shoes
trajectory.description: Released The Red Shoes, her seventh studio album, accompanied by a short film featuring Miranda Richardson and Lindsay Kemp; followed by a 12-year hiatus from recording.

trajectory.title: Aerial - return after 12 years
trajectory.description: Released Aerial, her first album in 12 years, a double album praised by critics for its ambition and intimacy, confirming her status as a reclusive genius.

trajectory.title: Before the Dawn concert residency
trajectory.description: Performed Before the Dawn, a 22-night residency at Hammersmith Apollo, her first live shows since the Tour of Life in 1979, receiving universal acclaim.

trajectory.title: 'Running Up That Hill' global resurgence
trajectory.description: After featuring in Netflix's Stranger Things, 'Running Up That Hill' became her second UK number-one single 44 years after her first, reaching number three on the US Billboard Hot 100.

name: Mark Webber
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Formula One debut at the 2002 Australian Grand Prix on March 3, 2002 at age 25, finishing fifth and scoring points — becoming the 51st driver in F1 history to score on debut and the first Australian F1 driver since 1994.
early_history_summary: Webber began karting at age 12-13 in Queanbeyan, Australia, buying a go-kart from a school friend's father. His father leased a petrol station and worked long hours to fund his racing. He won regional karting championships in 1992-93, moved to car racing in 1994, and progressed through Australian Formula Ford, British Formula Ford, FIA GT Championship with Mercedes AMG, and International Formula 3000 before reaching F1 in 2002.
family_context_summary: Born to middle-class parents in Queanbeyan, New South Wales. Father was a motorcycle enthusiast who leased a petrol station and worked long hours at a car dealer to fund Mark's karting. Maternal grandfather had a 2,500-acre farm where Mark drove motorbikes from age 4-5.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a motorcycle enthusiast and worked in fuel/automotive sectors, providing early exposure to motorsport culture. No professional racing background in family.
evidence_summary: Webber's path to F1 was built on years of progressive racing from karting in rural Australia to European formula racing. His father made significant financial sacrifices, leasing a petrol station and working extra jobs to fund karting. Andy Lawson built karts around Webber's frame, and Ralph Firman Sr. signed him to the Van Diemen factory team. Moving to London in 1995 placed him in the UK motorsport hub. His F1 debut at 25, scoring points for Minardi, was the culmination of a decade of systematic progression through racing categories.
starting_point: Born in 1976 in Queanbeyan, New South Wales, Australia; left Australia at 19 with no sponsors to pursue racing in England; won the Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch.
current_position: Australian former racing driver; FIA World Endurance Champion (2015) with Porsche; F1 pundit for Channel 4 and Network 10; driver manager; Officer of the Order of Australia.

trajectory.title: Formula Ford Festival winner
trajectory.description: Won the prestigious Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch after moving from Australia to the UK to pursue racing.

trajectory.title: FIA GT Championship runner-up
trajectory.description: Finished runner-up in the FIA GT Championship with AMG Mercedes, winning five of ten races alongside Bernd Schneider.

trajectory.title: F3000 runner-up and F1 test driver
trajectory.description: Finished second in International F3000 with Super Nova Racing and served as test driver for Benetton.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with Minardi

trajectory.title: First F1 podium at Monaco

trajectory.title: Third in World Championship

trajectory.title: Retirement from motorsport
trajectory.description: Retired from competitive motorsport, becoming a television pundit and driver manager.

name: Gianluigi Buffon
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Parma on November 19, 1995 at age 17, keeping a clean sheet against reigning champions AC Milan, and by 26 had become a World Cup-winning goalkeeper, Serie A champion, and the world's most expensive goalkeeper transfer.
early_history_summary: Buffon joined Parma's youth system in 1991 at age 13. He made his Serie A debut at 17 in November 1995 when first-choice keeper Luca Bucci was injured, keeping a clean sheet against AC Milan's star-studded attack including Baggio and Weah. He became Parma's starting goalkeeper the following season and won the Coppa Italia, UEFA Cup, and Italian Super Cup with Parma before his world-record transfer to Juventus in 2001.
family_context_summary: Born in Carrara, Tuscany. Both parents were physical education teachers — mother Maria Stella Masocco was a discus thrower and father Adriano was a weightlifter. Two sisters were also athletes. Athletic family environment with strong sporting genes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were PE teachers and competitive athletes (discus thrower and weightlifter). Family provided a deeply athletic environment and genetic predisposition for physical performance, though not football-specific.
evidence_summary: Buffon's extraordinary debut at 17 — keeping a clean sheet against AC Milan's world-class attack — was immediately recognized as exceptional by legends like Dino Zoff. Both parents were competitive athletes and PE teachers, providing a strong athletic foundation. The Parma youth system, one of Italy's finest academies, gave him elite training from age 13. Coach Nevio Scala's decision to debut him at 17 against Milan was a pivotal mentorship moment. His athletic family background and the Italian football pipeline combined with his prodigy-level talent to create an accelerated path to the top.
starting_point: Born in 1978 in Carrara, Italy; came from a family of athletes — his mother was a discus thrower and his father a weightlifter; joined Parma's youth academy.
current_position: Italian former footballer; retired in 2023 at age 45; widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time; 2006 World Cup winner; holds record for most Serie A appearances.

trajectory.title: Serie A debut for Parma
trajectory.description: Made his Serie A debut on November 19, 1995, keeping a clean sheet against reigning champions AC Milan.

trajectory.title: UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Cup, Coppa Italia, and Supercoppa Italiana with Parma, establishing himself as one of the world's best goalkeepers.

trajectory.description: Transferred to Juventus for €52.9 million, the world record fee for a goalkeeper, which stood for 17 years.

trajectory.title: Champions League final and UEFA Club Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Reached the Champions League final with Juventus (lost to AC Milan) and was named UEFA Club Footballer of the Year.

trajectory.title: World Cup winner

trajectory.title: Stayed with Juventus through relegation

trajectory.title: The Best FIFA Goalkeeper award
trajectory.description: Won the inaugural The Best FIFA Men's Goalkeeper award and was named Serie A Footballer of the Year after reaching another Champions League final.

trajectory.title: Moved to Paris Saint-Germain
trajectory.description: Signed with PSG at age 40, winning Ligue 1 and the Trophée des Champions in his only season in France.

trajectory.title: Return to Parma
trajectory.description: Returned to his boyhood club Parma, who had been relegated to Serie B, for a sentimental final spell.

trajectory.title: Retirement from football
trajectory.description: Retired at age 45 after a 28-year professional career with over 1,100 appearances and 176 caps for Italy.

name: George Weah
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for AS Monaco in 1988 at age 22 after being discovered by Arsène Wenger, was named African Footballer of the Year in 1989 at age 23, won the Coupe de France with Monaco in 1991, and helped Monaco reach the European Cup Winners' Cup final in 1992 before signing for PSG at age 26.
early_history_summary: Weah grew up in the Clara Town slum of Monrovia, Liberia, raised by his grandmother after his parents separated. He played street football and climbed through Liberian local clubs — Bong Range United, Mighty Barrolle, Invincible Eleven — before joining Cameroonian club Tonnerre Yaoundé in 1987. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who signed him for £12,000 in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Monrovia, Liberia, and raised in the Clara Town slum. Father William was a mechanic; mother Anna Quaye Weah died early. Raised by paternal grandmother Emma Klonjlaleh Brown. Extreme poverty; member of the Kru ethnic group from one of Liberia's poorest areas.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football or professional connections in family. Father was a mechanic. No domain-relevant transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Weah's path from Monrovia slums to European football was extraordinary. He had no family resources, no training facilities, and no football connections — he learned the game on dusty streets. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy spotted him and recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who became a father figure and mentor. Wenger's sustained coaching was transformative. Weah was named African Footballer of the Year at 23 in 1989. His extreme poverty and outsider status created the urgency and distinctive style that propelled him, but Wenger's mentorship was the critical catalyst that brought him to European football.
starting_point: Born in the Clara Town slum of Monrovia, Liberia; father was a mechanic and mother died early; raised by paternal grandmother in extreme poverty; member of the Kru ethnic group.
current_position: Former President of Liberia (2018-2024); living in Monrovia, Liberia; lost re-election in 2023; estimated net worth ~$30 million.

trajectory.title: Signed for AS Monaco
trajectory.description: Signed for AS Monaco by Arsene Wenger, who became a father figure and mentor, after being recommended by Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy.

trajectory.title: African Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named African Footballer of the Year for the first time, recognizing his explosive talent in European football.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Paris Saint-Germain
trajectory.description: Moved to PSG, where he won Division 1 in 1994 and became the top scorer of the 1994-95 UEFA Champions League.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Became the first and only African player to win both the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year; signed for AC Milan the same year.

trajectory.title: Serie A title with AC Milan
trajectory.description: Won the Serie A title with AC Milan in his first season, finishing as the club's top goalscorer under Fabio Capello; won Serie A again in 1999.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after spells at Chelsea, Manchester City, Marseille, and Al Jazira, ending an 18-year professional career.

trajectory.title: Elected to Liberian Senate
trajectory.description: Elected to the Liberian Senate representing Montserrado County with 78% of the vote, becoming the first Liberian international athlete elected to the legislature.

trajectory.title: Inaugurated as President of Liberia
trajectory.description: Sworn in as the 25th President of Liberia, becoming the first African former professional footballer to become a head of state.

trajectory.title: Left presidency after electoral defeat
trajectory.description: Left office after losing the 2023 presidential election to Joseph Boakai, peacefully transferring power and reinforcing Liberia's democratic process.

name: Klaus Ebner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Großer Österreichischer Jugendpreis (Austrian Youth Prize for Literature) in 1982 at age 18 for the novella 'Das Brandmal,' and again in 1988 for the novel 'Nils,' establishing early recognition as a literary talent.
early_history_summary: Ebner was born in Vienna and attended secondary school for eight years, where his first writing experiences began. At age twelve he wrote a short theater play rehearsed with school friends. He later submitted prose and poems to juvenile literature competitions together with his friend Peter Seifert. In 1982, at age 18, he was awarded the Großer Österreichischer Jugendpreis, and he began studying translation and Romance languages at the University of Vienna that same year while working for a literary circle and Viennese literature magazine.
family_context_summary: His mother Ingeborg worked as a hairdresser and his father Walter was a salesman in the entertainment electronics industry. The family was working-to-middle class with no documented literary connections.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental involvement in literature or publishing.
evidence_summary: Ebner began writing as a teenager in Vienna, submitting work to juvenile literature competitions with his friend Peter Seifert. At age 18 he won the Austrian Youth Prize for Literature, providing early professional recognition. He studied at the University of Vienna while participating in a literary circle and magazine. His family background — mother a hairdresser, father a salesman — provided no direct literary advantage. Vienna's cultural environment and his early immersion in multiple languages (German, French, Italian, later Catalan) were the main accelerants.

name: Peter Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: Received funding from the New Zealand Film Commission in 1986 (age 24-25) to complete his first feature film Bad Taste, which premiered at the 1988 Cannes Film Festival when he was 26, launching his professional filmmaking career.
early_history_summary: Jackson grew up in Pukerua Bay, New Zealand, and was given a Super 8 cine-camera by a family friend as a child. He began making short films with friends, teaching himself editing, visual effects, and makeup through trial and error. He left school at 16 and worked as a photo-engraver at the Evening Post newspaper for seven years, living at home and saving money for film equipment. He bought a 16mm camera and began shooting what became Bad Taste on weekends, eventually securing NZ Film Commission funding in 1986 to complete the film.
family_context_summary: Parents were Joan (née Ruck), a factory worker and housewife, and William 'Bill' Jackson, a wages clerk — both English immigrants. The family was working-class; a family friend gifted them a Super 8 camera with Peter in mind, which proved catalytic.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents had no film industry connections; however, a family friend provided the Super 8 camera that launched Jackson's filmmaking.
evidence_summary: Jackson began making films as a child in Pukerua Bay with a gifted Super 8 camera, teaching himself all aspects of filmmaking through trial and error. He worked seven years as a newspaper photo-engraver while living at home, saving for a 16mm camera to shoot Bad Taste on weekends. His working-class English immigrant parents had no film connections but supported his obsession. The NZ Film Commission funding in 1986 was the key institutional milestone, enabling him to quit his job and complete the film. His isolation in New Zealand, far from any film industry, forced self-reliance and DIY ingenuity that became his signature.
starting_point: Born in 1961 in Pukerua Bay, New Zealand; given a Super 8mm camera as a child; no formal film training; worked as a photo-engraver at a Wellington newspaper while making films on weekends.
current_position: New Zealand filmmaker; Sir Peter Jackson ONZ KNZM; fourth-highest-grossing film director of all time with over $6.5 billion worldwide; co-founder of Weta Digital.

name: Gheorghe Hagi
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Divizia A (Romanian top division) debut at age 17 in 1982-83 for FC Constanța, then scored 58 goals in 108 appearances for Sportul Studențesc between 1983 and 1986 (ages 18-21), becoming one of Romania's most prodigious young talents and drawing the attention of dictator Ceaușescu before transferring to Steaua București in 1986.
early_history_summary: Hagi was born in the village of Săcele near Constanța to a humble Aromanian family. He joined the FC Constanța youth academy at age 10 and was later pushed by the Romanian Football Federation to Luceafărul București for development. He made his first-team debut for FC Constanța at 17, scoring 7 goals in 18 games, and moved to Sportul Studențesc at 18, where his prolific scoring drew national attention and led to his transfer to Steaua București at 21.
family_context_summary: Hagi was born to Iancu and Chirata Hagi in the village of Săcele. His father was a construction worker earning approximately $83/month. His grandfather was an Aromanian shepherd who had fled Greece to Romania. The family was poor and moved to Constanța when Hagi was 7.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family involvement in professional football, though Hagi's grandfather was a shepherd and the family had Aromanian heritage.
evidence_summary: Hagi grew up in a poor Aromanian family in rural Romania, playing football in the streets with balls made from rags. He was discovered at a schoolyard by coach Iosif Bükössy, who noted his exceptional natural ability, and entered the FC Constanța youth academy at age 10. The Romanian Football Federation's development system placed him at Luceafărul București for elite training. He made his professional debut at 17 and became a prolific scorer by 21, aided by innate talent and intense dedication rather than family resources or connections. His humble background and the constraints of communist Romania created urgency and a distinctive playing style.
starting_point: Born in 1965 in Săcele, Romania; grew up in the Romanian football system; his talent drew the attention of dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu, who orchestrated his transfer to Steaua București.
current_position: Romanian football manager and former player; head coach of the Romania national team; founded Viitorul Constanța academy and club; nicknamed 'The Maradona of the Carpathians.'

name: Michele Alboreto
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Formula Three Championship in 1980 (age 23-24), made his Formula One debut with Tyrrell at the 1981 San Marino Grand Prix (age 24), and won his first F1 Grand Prix at the 1982 Caesars Palace Grand Prix in Las Vegas (age 25), establishing himself as a rising star in motorsport.
early_history_summary: Alboreto was born in Milan and built his first kart at 17 with his brother Carlo. He began racing in Formula Monza in 1976 with a car he and friends built themselves. He moved to Formula Italia in 1978 and then to Formula Three, winning the European F3 Championship in 1980 with four race wins. This led to his F1 debut with Tyrrell in 1981 and his first F1 victory at the end of the 1982 season.
family_context_summary: His father was a small-business owner (described as a mechanic in some sources); the family had no motorsport background. Alboreto had to earn his opportunities through determination and natural ability rather than financial backing, unlike many of his contemporaries.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family involvement in motorsport; the family had no racing background.
evidence_summary: Alboreto grew up in Milan with no motorsport family background. He built his first kart at 17 with his brother and progressed from Formula Monza (with a self-built car) to Formula Italia, then to the European F3 Championship, which he won in 1980. Ken Tyrrell spotted his talent and gave him an F1 drive in 1981. His middle-class background meant he lacked the financial backing of many competitors, making his rise through the Italian motorsport pipeline a product of talent and determination. The Lancia sportscar team and Euroracing provided additional elite-level experience that accelerated his development.
starting_point: Born in Milan, Italy in 1956 to a small-business owner father with no motorsport background; built his first kart at 17 with his brother Carlo and began racing locally.
current_position: Died on April 25, 2001 at age 44 in a testing crash at the Lausitzring in Germany; final role as an Audi sportscar driver.

name: Mo Yan
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first short story in a literary journal in 1981 at age 26, marking the beginning of his professional writing career while serving in the People's Liberation Army.
early_history_summary: Mo Yan was born Guan Moye in 1955 into a peasant family in Gaomi, Shandong Province. He withdrew from school at age 11 during the Cultural Revolution and worked in agriculture and later at a cotton processing factory. He joined the People's Liberation Army in 1976, where he began studying literature and writing. He was accepted to the PLA Academy of Art and Literature, and his first short story was published in a literary journal in 1981.
family_context_summary: Born into a peasant family in Gaomi, Shandong. His father received four years of education at a pre-revolutionary private school; his mother was illiterate. The family was classified as 'upper-middle peasant' during class struggle campaigns, which brought political discrimination. He was the youngest of four children.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental involvement in literature or the arts; his father was a farmer with basic classical education and his mother was illiterate.
evidence_summary: Mo Yan grew up in extreme rural poverty in Shandong Province, withdrawing from school at 11 during the Cultural Revolution and working in agriculture and a cotton factory. He joined the PLA in 1976, where access to a library and the post-Mao literary revival enabled him to begin writing. His first short story was published in 1981 at age 26. His family had no literary connections — his father was a farmer with basic education, his mother illiterate. The adversity of his upbringing — poverty, political discrimination, lack of formal schooling — became the raw material of his fiction, giving him a distinctive folk-rooted voice that later earned the Nobel Prize.

early_history_summary: Affleck was born in Berkeley, California, and raised in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He began acting professionally at age 7 through his mother's friendship with a local casting director, appearing in the PBS series The Voyage of the Mimi (1984-88) and several TV movies as a teenager. He met Matt Damon at age 8, and they later collaborated on the screenplay for Good Will Hunting while struggling to find acting work in their early twenties. The film was purchased by Miramax and released in 1997, winning them the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.
family_context_summary: His mother Christopher Anne 'Chris' Boldt was a Harvard-educated elementary school teacher. His father Timothy Byers Affleck was an aspiring playwright and actor who worked sporadically as a janitor, bartender, and carpenter while struggling with severe alcoholism. Parents divorced when Affleck was 11. The family was not wealthy, but grew up in Cambridge, Massachusetts, surrounded by arts and intellectual life.

evidence_summary: Affleck grew up in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where his mother's friendship with a casting director enabled early acting roles from age 7. His father was an aspiring playwright and stage manager who struggled with alcoholism, and the parents divorced when Affleck was 11, creating financial and emotional adversity. The defining early advantage was his childhood friendship with Matt Damon, who lived two blocks away and became his screenwriting partner and co-star in Good Will Hunting. The Cambridge arts environment, early professional acting experience, and the 1990s indie film wave all contributed to their Oscar-winning screenplay at ages 25-27. name: Elio de Angelis
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Italian Formula Three Championship in 1977 at age 19, made his Formula One debut with Shadow at the 1979 Argentine Grand Prix at age 20, and won his first F1 Grand Prix (1982 Austrian GP) at age 24, establishing himself as a top-tier racing driver by his mid-twenties.
early_history_summary: De Angelis was born in Rome to a wealthy family. He started karting at 14, finishing second in the World Championship in 1975 and winning the European title in 1976. He progressed to Formula Three in 1977, winning the Italian F3 championship at 19, and the prestigious Monaco F3 race in 1978. He entered Formula One with Shadow in 1979 as a pay driver funded by his father, then moved to Lotus in 1980 where he partnered Mario Andretti and later Nigel Mansell and Ayrton Senna.
family_context_summary: His father Giulio de Angelis was a wealthy real estate developer and construction company owner who also raced powerboats, winning multiple world championships in the 1960s and 1970s. The family was part of Rome's upper echelons; Elio was the eldest of four children and was known to be on a Red Brigades kidnapping target list, requiring bodyguards when visiting Rome.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a successful powerboat racer who took his sons to watch car races, giving them a lifelong love of motorsport. All three brothers won the national karting title, but only Elio was allowed to pursue racing professionally. His father funded his early single-seater career, including a reported $25,000 per race pay-driver deal with Shadow in F1.
evidence_summary: De Angelis was born into extreme wealth in Rome — his father Giulio was a real estate developer and champion powerboat racer who funded Elio's entire racing career. The father's motorsport passion meant Elio grew up watching car races and started karting at 14. His father paid for his F1 seat at Shadow (reportedly $25,000 per race), making him a pay driver initially. Despite the wealth, Elio demonstrated genuine talent: Italian F3 champion at 19, F1 debut at 20, first F1 win at 24. He was also a trained classical pianist of near-professional standard, multilingual, and educated at a Jesuit school for Roman aristocracy. The combination of unlimited family capital, direct domain immersion through his father, and natural talent created an exceptionally resourced pathway to F1.

name: Marita Koch

By age 26 she had set multiple world records and won the 1983 World Championship 200m title.
early_history_summary: Born in Wismar, East Germany, Koch displayed exceptional sprinting speed from childhood, defeating older boys in races. She began training under coach Wolfgang Meier at age 15 in 1972, moved to Rostock, and initially studied medicine before focusing full-time on athletics. She won her first international medals at the 1975 European Junior Championships and set her first indoor world record in 1977 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Koch was born in Wismar, East Germany. Family financial or professional background is not documented in reviewed sources. She was coached by Wolfgang Meier from age 15, whom she later married.

evidence_summary: Koch displayed exceptional natural sprinting speed from early childhood, defeating older boys in races. At 15, she began training under Wolfgang Meier, who coached her for her entire career. The East German state sports system provided an elite performance pipeline through SC Empor Rostock, with dedicated coaching, facilities, and support. She set her first world records at 20-21 and won European gold at 21. No family athletic background is documented, but her physical talent was exceptional and the GDR sports system was a frontier ecosystem for sprinting. name: John Lydon

The band released 'Anarchy in the U.K.' (November 1976), 'God Save the Queen' (May 1977), and the album 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' (28 October 1977) at age 21. He then founded Public Image Ltd in 1978 at age 22, releasing their debut album in 1978.
early_history_summary: Lydon grew up in a working-class Irish immigrant family in north London. He contracted spinal meningitis at age 7, causing hallucinations, memory loss, and a permanent spinal curvature that gave him his distinctive stare. He was expelled from school at 15 and attended Hackney and Kingsway colleges. In 1975, Malcolm McLaren spotted him at the SEX clothing shop due to his ragged look and orange hair, and recruited him as Sex Pistols lead vocalist after he tunelessly sang Alice Cooper's 'I'm Eighteen' on a jukebox.
family_context_summary: Lydon was born to working-class Irish immigrant parents in London. His father worked on building sites and oil rigs. The family lived in a two-room Victorian flat and later a council flat. He was the eldest of four brothers and cared for siblings due to his mother's illnesses.
parent_family_domain_summary: No music industry connections. Father worked in construction and on oil rigs. Working-class Irish immigrant family with no entertainment background.
evidence_summary: Lydon's path was driven by constraint-driven self-creation: working-class Irish immigrant background, spinal meningitis at 7 causing lasting physical and psychological effects, poverty, and no musical training. He was recruited to the Sex Pistols at 19 based on his look and attitude rather than musical skill. The London punk rock wave of 1976-1977 and McLaren's management/scene-building provided the structural context. The complementary team of Sex Pistols (Jones, Cook, Matlock) was crucial. His distinctive 'Lydon stare' resulted from meningitis, turning adversity into a defining visual asset.

Under Ronald Koeman, he became a starter and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title. He scored twice in his Champions League debut in September 2002. He grew up in the immigrant-heavy Rosengård area of Malmö.

His exceptional physical attributes (1.95m, athletic, acrobatic) combined with street-football technique gave him a distinctive skill set. Ajax's development ecosystem at age 19-20 accelerated his career, and he won the Eredivisie title in his first season. By 26, he had played for Ajax, Juventus, and Inter Milan, winning multiple league titles and individual awards.

He moved to McLaren in 2002 and won his first Grand Prix in 2003.

At 16, he left school and enrolled in a mechanics course.

evidence_summary: Räikkönen began karting at 10 in Espoo, Finland. Starr, and was discovered by CBS Records executive Tommy Mottola in 1988, who signed her to Columbia Records.
family_context_summary: Carey's mother Patricia (née Hickey) was a former opera singer and vocal coach of Irish descent who directly trained Mariah from childhood. Her mother's family disowned her for marrying a Black man.

Despite financial hardship and racial discrimination after her parents' divorce, Carey leveraged her mother's musical domain expertise and moved to New York City, the center of the American music industry. Her discovery by CBS Records executive Tommy Mottola and signing to Columbia Records provided major-label distribution and production resources. Her songwriting partnership with Ben Margulies produced the demo that led to her breakthrough.

name: Richard Clayderman
milestone_by_age_26: Recorded 'Ballade pour Adeline' in 1976 at age 23, which became a massive international hit selling millions of copies and launching a career that has sold over 120 million records worldwide.
early_history_summary: Born Philippe Pagès in Paris, Clayderman learned piano from his father, a piano and accordion teacher, starting at age three or four. He was accepted into the Conservatoire de Paris at age twelve, where he won acclaim. Financial difficulties from his father's illness forced him to leave the classical path and work as a bank clerk and accompanist for French singers including Johnny Hallyday and Michel Sardou. In 1976, at age 23, he was auditioned by producers Olivier Toussaint and Paul de Senneville and selected to record 'Ballade pour Adeline.'
family_context_summary: Clayderman's father was a piano and accordion teacher who taught him piano from age three or four in their home in a Paris suburb. The family lived modestly; a piano was always present in the apartment for the father's teaching. Father's illness caused financial difficulties that ended Clayderman's classical conservatory career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a piano and accordion teacher who provided direct, sustained piano instruction from age three. This is a strong family-domain advantage in piano performance. The father's conservatory connections helped Clayderman gain admission to the Conservatoire de Paris at age twelve.
evidence_summary: Clayderman's path to recording 'Ballade pour Adeline' at age 23 was built on a foundation of family-domain apprenticeship: his father, a piano and accordion teacher, taught him from age three, and his conservatory connections secured Clayderman's admission to the prestigious Conservatoire de Paris at age twelve. Over a decade of intensive classical training gave him a technically refined but accessible piano style. His father's illness forced him out of the classical path and into accompanist work, which paradoxically built his professional network and versatile repertoire. Producers Toussaint and de Senneville recognized his soft touch, good technique, and marketable appearance.

evidence_summary: Kaurismäki came to film relatively late after working manual labor jobs and studying media at the University of Tampere. His directorial debut Crime and Punishment (1983) at age 26 established his minimalist style. The brother collaboration was the dominant early advantage. His working-class background and late entry into film represent a modest constraint-driven path.

evidence_summary: O'Connor endured a severely abusive childhood in Dublin, including placement in a Magdalene laundry institution at 15 where a nun gave her a guitar and music lessons. She recorded with In Tua Nua at 15, formed Ton Ton Macoute at 17, and was signed to Ensign Records through the Dublin music scene. Her debut album The Lion and the Cobra (1987) at age 20 was an international sensation earning a Grammy nomination. Her manager Fachtna Ó Ceallaigh, formerly of U2's Mother Records, connected her to the Dublin music ecosystem. The extreme adversity of her childhood was a defining catalyst for her artistic output.

early_history_summary: Rossi was born in Urbino, Italy, and moved to Tavullia as a child. The son of former motorcycle racer Graziano Rossi, he began riding at a very young age. In 1993, former world champion Paolo Pileri gave him his first 125cc motorcycle ride, and he competed in the 125cc Italian Sport Production Championship. He made his Grand Prix debut in 1996 at age 17 and won the 125cc World Championship in 1997.
family_context_summary: Son of former motorcycle racer Graziano Rossi. Family moved to Tavullia when he was a child. Mother Stefania was concerned for his safety, directing him to kart racing before motorcycles. His half-brother Luca Marini also became a motorcycle racer.

Italy's position as a motorcycle racing powerhouse provided a frontier geography advantage. His family's racing background was the dominant early advantage.

He signed with the label Dejfitts Plays in May 2007 at age 17, remixed tracks for artists like Robyn and Dizzee Rascal, and had a modest European hit with 'Seek Bromance' in 2010 before 'Levels' exploded globally in 2011.

evidence_summary: Avicii's rise was driven by early adoption of online music communities (Laidback Luke forum, Myspace) for feedback and distribution, combined with self-taught production skills using FL Studio from age 16. He rode the massive EDM wave of the early 2010s, with 'Levels' (2011) becoming a defining track of the era. His mother's career as an actress and his brother's DJing provided early cultural exposure to performance and music, though his production skills were largely self-developed through online platforms.

The family lived in reasonably comfortable conditions before the bankruptcy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Her father was a jeweler, not connected to the music industry. No parental music domain expertise was documented.
evidence_summary: Shakira demonstrated extraordinary early talent, writing poetry at 4 and songs at 8, and belly dancing from age 4 after hearing Arabic music at a restaurant. A local theater producer convinced Sony Music Colombia to audition her at 13, leading to a three-album deal. After two commercial failures, she asserted creative control and broke through with Pies Descalzos at 18, selling 5M+ copies. Her father's bankruptcy at her age 8 created financial adversity, but also seemed to catalyze her drive. By 24, Laundry Service sold 13M+ copies globally. No family music connections or financial advantages were documented; her rise was largely self-created through prodigy-level talent and persistence.

name: Mikhail Khodorkovsky
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bank Menatep in 1989 at age 26, one of the first privately owned commercial banks in Russia, after establishing a successful import-export business and the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development in 1987 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Khodorkovsky graduated from the Mendeleev Institute of Chemical Technology in 1986 and became deputy head of the Komsomol at his university. Leveraging Komsomol connections during perestroika, he founded the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development in 1987, expanded into computer import-export, and acquired a banking license in 1989 to form Bank Menatep.
family_context_summary: Both parents were chemical engineers at a factory making measuring instruments in Moscow. They were middle-class, well-educated Soviets who silently opposed communism but kept this from their son.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were chemical engineers but had no business or financial domain expertise to transfer. Khodorkovsky followed their path initially by studying chemical engineering before pivoting to business.
evidence_summary: Khodorkovsky leveraged his position as deputy head of the Komsomol at the Mendeleev Institute to access the nascent private enterprise opportunities created by Gorbachev's perestroika reforms. In 1987 at age 24, he founded the Youth Centre for Scientific and Technical Development, which provided market research and technology brokering. By 1989 at age 26, he had acquired a banking license and formed Bank Menatep, one of Russia's first private commercial banks, with several business partners including Leonid Nevzlin. His parents were factory engineers with no business background; his advantage came from institutional positioning within the Komsomol during a unique historical window.
starting_point: Born in 1963 in Moscow; son of two engineers; studied at the Mendeleyev Chemistry Institute; began his career in the Komsomol (Communist Party youth organization) apparatus during the Soviet era.
current_position: Exiled Russian businessman, oligarch, and opposition activist; resides in London; founded Open Russia to promote civil society; was Russia's richest man before his imprisonment.

He moved to Rosario Central where he scored 85 goals in 105 matches, then transferred to Valencia in 1976, where he became La Liga's top scorer twice.

evidence_summary: Kempes grew up in Bell Ville, a town famously known as Argentina's 'national capital of football' for its ball manufacturing industry. He started playing at age 7, joined the Talleres reserves at 14, and debuted professionally for Instituto at 19 alongside Ossie Ardiles. His prolific goalscoring — 11 goals in 13 games for Instituto, 85 in 105 for Rosario Central — earned him a transfer to Valencia in 1976 at age 22, where he became La Liga's top scorer twice. name: David Beckham
milestone_by_age_26: Won the FA Youth Cup with Manchester United's Class of '92 in May 1992 and made his first-team debut on 23 September 1992 at age 17, launching a career that by age 26 included six Premier League titles, two FA Cups, and the 1999 UEFA Champions League.
early_history_summary: Beckham signed schoolboy forms with Manchester United on his 14th birthday in 1989 and a YTS contract in July 1991. He was part of the Class of '92 that won the FA Youth Cup, scoring in the final. He made his first-team debut as a substitute in a League Cup match in September 1992 and signed professional terms in January 1993. He became a first-team regular by 1995-96 and a global star by the late 1990s.
family_context_summary: Son of Sandra (née West), a hairdresser, and David Edward Alan 'Ted' Beckham, a kitchen fitter. Working-class family in Leytonstone, London. Parents were fanatical Manchester United supporters who travelled 200 miles to home matches.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father coached Beckham's local youth team Ridgeway Rovers and was a devoted Manchester United fan, providing direct football immersion from childhood. No professional football background in family.
evidence_summary: Beckham was immersed in football from childhood by his fanatical Manchester United-supporting parents, with his father coaching his local youth team. He joined Manchester United's academy at 14, was coached by Eric Harrison alongside the Class of '92 (Giggs, Scholes, Neville, Butt), won the FA Youth Cup at 17, and made his first-team debut the same year. The elite academy pipeline and exceptional peer group were the dominant early advantages. By age 26 he had won six Premier League titles and the Champions League.

name: Hans Zimmer
milestone_by_age_26: Composed his first film score for 'Moonlighting' (1982), a Palme d'Or-nominated Channel 4 film, at age 24-25, and co-founded Lillie Yard Studio with film composer Stanley Myers that same year.
early_history_summary: Zimmer was largely self-taught, playing piano from age 3 but rejecting formal lessons. Inspired by Ennio Morricone's score for 'Once Upon a Time in the West' at around age 12, he moved to London as a teenager. He wrote advertising jingles for Air-Edel Associates in the mid-1970s, played keyboards with the Buggles (appearing in the 'Video Killed the Radio Star' video in 1979), and worked with various new wave bands. He found a mentor in film composer Stanley Myers, with whom he co-founded Lillie Yard Studio and began working on film scores in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Frankfurt, West Germany. Father died when Zimmer was six years old, which intensified his commitment to music. Mother was a classically trained pianist who facilitated a musical environment. He attended boarding school in Switzerland before moving to London as a teenager.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a classically trained pianist who created a musical home environment. Father encouraged his innovative approach to music before his death when Zimmer was six. No film industry connections in family.
evidence_summary: Zimmer was a self-taught musician inspired by Morricone's film scores from age 12. After his father's death when he was six, music became his refuge. He moved to London as a teen, wrote jingles, played in bands including the Buggles, and found a pivotal mentor in film composer Stanley Myers. Together they founded Lillie Yard Studio in 1982, and Zimmer composed his first film score for 'Moonlighting' that year at age 24-25. His breakthrough with 'Rain Man' came later in 1988 at age 31, but the first film score and studio founding represent a material milestone by 26.
starting_point: Born in Frankfurt, Germany; father was an engineer and businessman who died when Zimmer was a child; mother was a musician. Grew up in a household without strong musical training but was largely self-taught.

name: Jacques Villeneuve

early_history_summary: The son of Ferrari F1 driver Gilles Villeneuve, Jacques grew up traveling the racing circuit with his family and moved to Monaco at age seven. After his father was killed in a racing accident in 1982, he attended boarding school in Switzerland. He began racing at 17 under an Andorran license in Italy, progressed through Italian and Japanese Formula Three, then moved to the Toyota Atlantic Championship and CART IndyCar racing, winning the Indy 500 and championship in 1995 before moving to F1 with Williams.
family_context_summary: Son of Formula One driver Gilles Villeneuve, who moved the family from Quebec to Monaco in 1978. After Gilles was killed in a 1982 racing accident, Jacques was raised by his mother and attended boarding school in Switzerland. The family remained in Monaco, providing a European base.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Gilles Villeneuve was a Ferrari Formula One driver; uncle Jacques-Joseph Villeneuve was also a racing driver. Jacques grew up immersed in the racing world from birth, traveling to races in a motorhome and living in F1 paddocks.
evidence_summary: Villeneuve was born into a racing dynasty: his father Gilles was a Ferrari F1 driver and his uncle was also a professional racer. He grew up in F1 paddocks and moved to Monaco at age seven, giving him direct domain immersion from birth. After his father's death in 1982, he still benefited from the Villeneuve name and racing network, which opened doors in Italian F3 and beyond. His progression through the elite motorsport pipeline (Italian F3, Japanese F3, Toyota Atlantic, CART, F1) was accelerated by his family background. Winning the Indy 500 and IndyCar championship at 24 and the F1 World Championship at 26 were clear material milestones.
starting_point: Born in Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec, Canada in 1971; son of Ferrari F1 driver Gilles Villeneuve, who was killed in a racing accident in 1982; raised in Monaco and attended boarding school in Switzerland before beginning racing at 17.

name: John McEnroe
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first U.S. Open singles title in 1979 at age 20, becoming the youngest U.S. champion in 31 years; reached Wimbledon semifinals at 18 in 1977 as a qualifier, won the NCAA singles title in 1978, and won four Grand Slam singles titles and reached world No. 1 by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Wiesbaden, West Germany to an American Air Force officer father, McEnroe grew up in Douglaston, Queens, New York. He began playing tennis at age eight at the Douglaston Club and was enrolled at the Port Washington Tennis Academy on Long Island. As an 18-year-old amateur qualifier in 1977, he reached the Wimbledon semifinals. He won the NCAA singles title at Stanford in 1978, then turned professional, winning his first U.S. Open in 1979.
family_context_summary: Born to a U.S. Air Force officer father who later became an advertising agent and then a lawyer; the family settled in Douglaston, Queens, an upper middle class community. His father's dual career provided financial stability for tennis training.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was in the U.S. Air Force and later became a lawyer; no tennis background in the family. However, the family's upper middle class status in Queens provided access to the Douglaston Club and Port Washington Tennis Academy.
evidence_summary: McEnroe benefited from an upper middle class upbringing in Queens that gave him access to the Douglaston Club and the elite Port Washington Tennis Academy, a major American tennis pipeline. His father's stable career as a military officer-turned-lawyer provided the financial basis for serious training. As a teenager he won the French Open junior title and at 18 became the youngest Wimbledon semifinalist as a qualifier. His NCAA title at Stanford in 1978 and immediate professional success, including the 1979 U.S. Open at age 20, were clear material milestones by 26. name: Gerhard Berger

early_history_summary: Born in Wörgl, Austria, Berger grew up around his father Johann's trucking company, driving trucks from a young age. He raced AlfaSuds and Formula Ford before moving to German and European Formula Three, where he was a multiple race winner. ATS brought him into Formula One in 1984, and he moved to Arrows for a full season in 1985.

evidence_summary: Berger grew up around his father's trucking company in Austria, driving trucks from a young age which gave him unusual early driving experience. He progressed through AlfaSuds, Formula Ford, and German/European Formula Three before making his F1 debut at age 24 in 1984 with ATS. By age 26 he was a full-season F1 driver with Arrows. name: Monica Seles
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1990 French Open at age 16, becoming the youngest-ever French Open champion, and reached world No. 1 ranking in March 1991 at age 17. By age 26 she had won 9 Grand Slam singles titles.
early_history_summary: Born in Novi Sad, Yugoslavia, Seles began playing tennis at age five under her father's coaching. At age 11 she won the Junior Orange Bowl in Miami, catching the attention of Nick Bollettieri. She moved to the US in early 1986 to train at the Bollettieri Academy, turned pro in 1989 at age 15, and won her first Grand Slam at the 1990 French Open at age 16.
family_context_summary: Father was a professional cartoonist employed at Dnevnik and Magyar Szo newspapers in Yugoslavia. He coached Monica in tennis from age five. The family relocated from Yugoslavia to the US in 1986 to support her training at the Bollettieri Academy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father coached Seles in tennis from age five; later her coach was Jelena Gencic before moving to the Bollettieri Academy. The family made significant sacrifices to relocate from Yugoslavia to Florida for her tennis career.
evidence_summary: Seles began tennis at age five under her father's coaching in Yugoslavia. At 11 she won the Junior Orange Bowl, attracting Nick Bollettieri's attention. The family relocated to Florida in 1986 so she could train at the Bollettieri Academy. She turned pro at 15 in 1989, won her first Grand Slam at the 1990 French Open at 16 (youngest ever), and reached world No. 1 at 17. Her father's early coaching, the Bollettieri pipeline, and the family's relocation were key early advantages. By age 26 she had won 9 Grand Slam titles.

name: Sid Vicious
milestone_by_age_26: Was the bassist for the Sex Pistols during the release of 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' (October 1977), one of the most influential punk rock albums ever recorded.
early_history_summary: Born Simon John Ritchie in Lewisham, London, to a single mother who sold marijuana, Vicious grew up in turbulent circumstances across Kent and Hackney. He met John Lydon at technical college in 1973 and became part of the 'Four Johns' squatting circle. He was a regular at Malcolm McLaren and Vivienne Westwood's SEX clothing shop, the hub of the emerging London punk scene. He joined the Sex Pistols as bassist in early 1977 at age 19, replacing Glen Matlock, and appeared on their landmark debut album released in October 1977.
family_context_summary: Vicious was raised by a single mother, Anne Beverley, who dropped out of school and sold marijuana to get by. His father abandoned the family shortly after his birth. His stepfather died when he was young. The family lived in working-class conditions across Kent and East London.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a semi-professional trombone player on the London jazz scene, but abandoned the family. No evidence of musical training or industry connections transferred from parents.
evidence_summary: Vicious's fame was driven by proximity to the London punk scene centered on McLaren and Westwood's SEX shop, his friendship with John Lydon, and the explosive cultural wave of punk rock in 1977. He had no musical training and was famously unable to play bass competently, yet his persona and the Sex Pistols' cultural moment made him an icon. His turbulent, impoverished upbringing with a drug-dealing mother created the conditions for his punk identity. He died at 21, so all achievements were before 26. The milestone is material despite his limited musical contribution, as the album is independently verifiable and culturally landmark.

family_context_summary: Father R.K. Shekhar was a film score composer and conductor for Malayalam films who died when Rahman was 9, forcing the family into financial hardship. Rahman's mother used Shekhar's industry connections to get the young Rahman work in recording sessions.
evidence_summary: Rahman's father R.K. Shekhar was a film score composer for Malayalam cinema, providing direct domain exposure and studio access from age 4. After Shekhar's death when Rahman was 9, the family faced severe financial hardship, and Rahman's mother leveraged Shekhar's industry connections to get the boy work as a keyboard player at recording sessions from age 12. This gave him roughly 13 years of professional studio experience before his breakthrough with Roja at 25. The adversity of losing his father and needing to support his family created urgency and deep immersion in the craft.

name: Angus Young
milestone_by_age_26: By age 19, Young co-founded AC/DC and released their debut album High Voltage (1975) which reached #7 in Australia; by 25, Back in Black (1980) became one of the best-selling albums of all time.
early_history_summary: Born in Glasgow to a large working-class family that emigrated to Sydney, Angus grew up surrounded by music — older brothers George (Easybeats star), Alex, and Malcolm were all musicians. He began playing guitar as a young teenager, joined local bands Kantuckee and Tantrum, and co-founded AC/DC with brother Malcolm in November 1973 at age 18. With production by brother George and Harry Vanda, AC/DC released their debut album in February 1975 and quickly became stars in Australia.

George Young's success with the Easybeats and his production partnership with Harry Vanda provided direct industry access, mentorship, and production infrastructure for AC/DC.
evidence_summary: Angus Young grew up in a remarkably musical working-class family where three older brothers became professional musicians. Brother George Young's stardom with the Easybeats provided a direct template, industry connections through Albert Productions, and production mentorship via the Vanda & Young partnership. Angus began playing guitar as a young teen, formed AC/DC with brother Malcolm at 18, and released their debut album at 19 with George producing. The sibling collaboration with Malcolm as cofounder and George as producer-mentor was the dominant early advantage. By 25, Back in Black made AC/DC one of the biggest rock bands in history.

He broke into Dynamo's first team at 18 under legendary coach Valeriy Lobanovskyi and quickly became a key player, scoring 60 goals in 117 league appearances before transferring to AC Milan in 1999 for £18m at age 23.

evidence_summary: Shevchenko's early success was driven by the Dynamo Kyiv academy pipeline, which he entered at age 9-10, and the elite coaching of Oleksandr Shpakov and later Valeriy Lobanovskyi. His exceptional speed and finishing ability were recognized early — he was top scorer at the Ian Rush Cup at 14 and starred at an Italian tournament at 13. The Chernobyl disaster nearly ended his football career but his coach convinced him to return. By 18 he was scoring in the Champions League; by 23 he was sold to AC Milan for £18m. No family football background or financial advantage is documented.

evidence_summary: Moore's father ran a ballroom and bought him his first guitar at 10, giving him early exposure to live music and performance. His partnership with Phil Lynott in Skid Row and later Thin Lizzy provided a complementary collaborator. The late 1960s blues rock boom created a structural wave that enabled a teenage guitarist to secure a major label deal.

His first album 'MKWAJU' came in 1981 and his landmark Miyazaki collaboration began in 1984 (age 33-34), but his professional broadcast composing credits by age 24-26 represent a material, independently verifiable milestone.
